# L2 · Chat template

**Can the small program that formats every prompt change what the model is told, or run code?**

Before your message reaches the model, a hidden Jinja2 program (the chat template) wraps it in the model's expected format. It ships inside the model file (GGUF metadata or tokenizer_config.json) and runs on every single request. A few extra lines can quietly add instructions whenever a trigger word appears, without touching the weights.

*Example:* A GGUF that answers normally until a user mentions a certain product, then starts giving wrong answers and inserting attacker links.

## L2.01

### Chat-template backdoor (conditional hidden instructions)

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2025-07-09, Pillar Security

A few lines of Jinja2 added to the template check the user's message for a trigger phrase and, if found, prepend attacker instructions as a system message. Weights are unchanged and benign prompts render byte-for-byte identical, so evaluations and hub scans pass.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-24 | Paper v4: 18 models, 7 families, 4 engines; triggered accuracy falls from ~90% to ~15%, attacker-URL emission above 80%; tool-use hijack across 3,868 agent episodes; passes all automated hub scans; sandboxing the template engine does not stop it. | [Pillar Security + Fujitsu, arXiv 2602.04653](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04653) |
| 2026-02-19 | Large-scale look at GGUF templates on Hugging Face; mismatches mostly benign runtime differences, i.e. few signs of in-the-wild use. | [Splunk](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/gguf-llm-security-inference-time-poisoning-templates.html) |
| 2026-02-10 | Validation across 18 models and llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang. | [Pillar Security](https://www.pillar.security/blog/from-discovery-to-large-scale-validation-chat-template-backdoors-across-18-models-and-4-engines) |
| 2025-07-09 | Inference-time backdoors via poisoned GGUF chat templates first described. **(first)** | [Pillar Security](https://www.pillar.security/blog/llm-backdoors-at-the-inference-level-the-threat-of-poisoned-templates) |

## L2.02

### Template injection (SSTI) to code execution

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2024-05-16, Checkmarx

If the runner renders the model's template with an unsandboxed Jinja2 environment, the template can reach Python internals and run commands on the server.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-22 | SGLang CVE-2026-5760: template from a GGUF rendered unsandboxed; reachable through the rerank endpoint. | [Cloud Security Alliance research note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-sglang-cve-2026-5760-gguf-rce-20260422-csa/) |
| 2024-05-16 | 'Llama Drama' CVE-2024-34359 in llama-cpp-python: model metadata template rendered without a sandbox; fixed in 0.2.72. **(first)** | [Checkmarx](https://checkmarx.com/blog/llama-drama-critical-vulnerability-cve-2024-34359-threatening-your-software-supply-chain) |

## L2.03

### Chat-template token spoofing in untrusted content

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-04-20, Chang, Jun, Lee

Untrusted text (a web page, a tool result) is formatted with the model's own role tags so the model treats it as a higher-authority turn. Chains into L6 prompt injection.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-20 | ChatInject: success rises from 5.18% to 32.05% on AgentDojo and 15.13% to 45.90% on InjecAgent; transfers to closed models (ICLR 2026; earliest verified). **(first)** | [Chang, Jun, Lee](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/2a48e053db5f0cd57015a33bbc3f794b-Abstract-Conference.html) |

## L2.04

### Clean template shown, poisoned template downloaded

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2025-07-09, Pillar Security

The hub's web view shows one template while the downloadable GGUF carries another, so a human review of the page misses the change.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-07-09 | Described alongside the original template-backdoor research. **(first)** | [Pillar Security](https://www.pillar.security/blog/llm-backdoors-at-the-inference-level-the-threat-of-poisoned-templates) |
